platform: Scopus web interface, advanced search (no API key; amendment AM-7)
status: An addition to the 2026-09-13 round, not a new review. Scopus was a declared gap in that round because its API returned HTTP 401 without a key. It is searched here through the institutional web interface, and the gap closes for the three query subjects below and for nothing else.
peer_review_of_search: none; no information specialist reviewed these strategies
language_restriction: none applied at the database level; eligibility is limited to English or Czech full text and that restriction is declared
date_limits: no lower limit; upper limit is the execution date, 2026-10-07
deduplication: within-Scopus duplicates are impossible (the EID is unique); the cross-database merge against the PubMed and ACL pool is recorded in pool-summary.json

who_ran_it.queries_written_by: assistant, from the three layers of the parent protocol
who_ran_it.handed_over_as: a local handover note listing the three query strings verbatim, the instruction to apply no filters, and the instruction not to edit, sort or truncate the export; kept out of the repository as working material
who_ran_it.evidence_for_that: the handover note was written at 2026-10-07T11:35:39 local time and the first export was downloaded at 2026-10-07T11:43:40; the strings in it are reproduced here unchanged.
who_ran_it.what_is_retrospective: this log was written on 2026-10-07 after the exports arrived, so its counts and checksums are recorded after the fact. The queries are not, and the counts are properties of files that cannot be re-run anyway.

deviations.what: the hit count each query reported in the interface was not captured
deviations.effect: total_records is the export row count, a lower bound. Whether an export is complete cannot be verified from the file alone.
deviations.remedy: the three numbers can be read off the interface and filled in; until then the field says what it is

deviations.effect: all 10 of its records are inside the 1373 of scopus-llm-docs and all 10 satisfy that query, so it is a narrower export of the same search and adds no record. It is not logged as a fourth search, because the query that produced it was not recorded, and it is counted nowhere.

deviations.what: the investigator ran the searches, not a script
deviations.effect: these searches are not re-runnable from this repository, unlike the PubMed and ACL ones. The query strings, the date, the files and their checksums are what makes them auditable.

deviations.what: the three queries are not translations of the PubMed set
deviations.effect: they cover the same three subjects in Scopus syntax over a wider field set. Record counts between the two databases are therefore not comparable query by query, and no such comparison is reported.

searches.platform: Scopus web interface, advanced search, institutional access (Masaryk University)
searches.subject_matter: Psychotherapy and counselling documentation itself: the direct layer, the same subject matter as pubmed-direct and acl-direct.
searches.query_as_run: TITLE-ABS-KEY((psychotherap* OR counsel* OR "mental health") AND ("progress note*" OR "session summar*" OR "therapy note*" OR "clinical documentation" OR "case note*"))
searches.fields_searched: TITLE-ABS-KEY: title, abstract, author keywords and indexed keywords. This is wider than the Title/Abstract of the PubMed queries, so a Scopus query reaches records its PubMed counterpart cannot.
searches.executed_by: investigator, in the browser; the assistant holds no Scopus credential
searches.executed_utc_basis: not recorded. The search was run by hand and the interface timestamps nothing; the download time of the export file is recorded instead and is the closest fact available.
searches.filters_applied: none; no date, language, document-type or subject-area limit
searches.total_records_basis: the number of rows in the export. The hit count the interface reported for this query was not written down, so this is what is in hand: a lower bound on what the query returned, not the query's reported total.
searches.download_complete_basis: unverified. Completeness could be asserted only against the interface's reported hit count, which was not captured. No export reaches the 2000-record ceiling at which Scopus refuses to export everything, so truncation is unlikely, and unlikely is not verified.
searches.export_format: CSV with abstracts, author and indexed keywords, DOI and EID
searches.query_identified_by: 98.0% of this file's rows satisfy its own query and under 4% satisfy either other query. The shortfall from 100% is the local re-implementation of Scopus truncation and phrase matching, not a mixed file.
